Hi Tom —

Appreciate the heads up and the spreadsheet. We can add eu-west3 to the subprocessor registry and push a short Exhibit B addendum that lists the new endpoint and clarifies the transfer mechanism. From a high level: Redwood will continue to rely on SCCs for transfers from the EU and include an explicit processor-to-processor transfer clause for any failover routing. Naomi — can you confirm wording?

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood to share redlined Exhibit B (tracks changes only) — attached.
- Once legal signs off, we’ll issue a DocuSign envelope for re-execution of the DPA addendum and Exhibit B.
- We’ll attach an executed PDF to the HubSpot deal and share the updated subprocessor registry export.

Can you confirm the MediCore signatory (Sanjay?) and whether they want Acrobat/AdobeSign or DocuSign? We can support either.

Thanks — aiming for end-of-week.

Karthik / Marissa —

I reviewed the redlines. A few notes for the exhibit we’ll send:
- Add explicit language that GCP eu-west3 is used solely for failover and warm-standby; specify retention/ingress endpoints.
- Confirm that the EU -> EU routing remains within SCC protections; where US-origin data could be routed, add a transfer mechanism fallback (SCC + documented lawful basis).
- Add a short Audit Access clause (30 days notice for audit requests) — MediCore requested log-retention details in an earlier thread.

I put tracked comments in Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx. If MediCore insists on an alternate transfer mechanism (e.g., UK Addendum), we’ll need their legal to say so; otherwise we’ll stick with SCCs and a processor-to-processor clause.

Naomi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Internal] Please do not send the vendor the draft until we incorporate the audit clause and the eu-west3 specifics. Marissa — can you coordinate the change log for the customer-facing exhibit?
